question: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. Find a non-zero vector $\vec{c}$ perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.
explanation:
A vector perpendicular to both $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i} (2 \times 2 - 1 \times (-1)) - \hat{j}(1 \times 2 - 1 \times 2) + \hat{k}(1 \times (-1) - 2 \times 2)$

$= \hat{i}(4 + 1) - \hat{j}(2-2) + \hat{k}(-1-4)$

$= 5\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$

$= 5(\hat{i} - \hat{k})$

So, $\boxed{\hat{i} - \hat{k}}$ is a unit vector perpendicular to both, but any non-zero multiple is also perpendicular.
